chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَائِذٍ عَنْ أَبِي سَلَمَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ:

translations.en: Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh narrated from Abū Salamah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

chunks.arabic_text: فِي رَجُلَيْنِ مَمْلُوكَيْنِ مُفَوَّضٍ إِلَيْهِمَا يَشْتَرِيَانِ وَ يَبِيعَانِ بِأَمْوَالِ مَوَالِيهِمَا فَكَانَ بَيْنَهُمَا كَلَامٌ فَٱقْتَتَلَا فَخَرَجَ هَٰذَا يَعْدُو إِلَى مَوْلَى هَٰذَا وَ هَٰذَا إِلَى مَوْلَى هَٰذَا وَ هُمَا فِي ٱلْقُوَّةِ سَوَاءٌ

translations.en: Concerning two slave men who had been entrusted with authority to buy and sell using the wealth of their masters. A dispute arose between them, and they fought. Then this one ran to the master of that one, and that one to the master of this one, while they were equal in strength.

chunks.arabic_text: فَٱشْتَرَى هَٰذَا مِنْ مَوْلَى هَٰذَا ٱلْعَبْدِ وَ ذَهَبَ هَٰذَا فَٱشْتَرَى هَٰذَا مِنْ مَوْلَاهُ وَ جَاءَ هَٰذَا وَ أَخَذَ بِتَلْبِيبِ هَٰذَا وَ أَخَذَ هَٰذَا بِتَلْبِيبِ هَٰذَا وَ قَالَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا لِصَاحِبِهِ أَنْتَ عَبْدِي قَدِ ٱشْتَرَيْتُكَ

translations.en: So this one purchased that slave from the master of the other, and that one went and purchased this one from his master. Then this one came and seized the collar of that one, and that one seized the collar of this one, and each of them said to his companion: “You are my slave; I have purchased you.”

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ يُحْكَمُ بَيْنَهُمَا مِنْ حَيْثُ ٱفْتَرَقَا فَيُذْرَعُ ٱلطَّرِيقُ فَأَيُّهُمَا كَانَ أَقْرَبَ فَٱلَّذِي أَخَذَ فِيهِ هُوَ ٱلَّذِي سَبَقَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَبْعَدُ وَ إِنْ كَانَا سَوَاءً فَهُمَا رَدٌّ عَلَى مَوَالِيهِمَا

translations.en: He عليه السلام said: “Judgment is to be made between them from the point where they separated. The road is to be measured, and whichever of them was nearer, then the one who took that route is the one who preceded the one who was farther away. And if they were equal, then both are returned to their masters.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about two authorized slave agents who each hurried to buy the other from his master after a quarrel. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rules that the matter is determined by measuring the distance from the point of separation, giving precedence to the one who had the shorter route; if both are equal, the attempted purchases cancel out and both are returned to their original masters.
en.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rule when two agents each claim to have purchased the other first?

key_terms.يَشْتَرِيَانِ: they both buy in the course of trade
key_terms.بِتَلْبِيبِ: by the collar or upper garment at the neck
